query: What does the family chat reveal about Chidi's role in family discussions?
gold: Chidi participates infrequently and briefly, but his messages carry decisive weight. He typically arrives late to a conversation that has already been debated at length, then issues a short statement that ends the discussion. In Session 2, when the family had been going back and forth about Ngozi's cooking, Chidi arrived late with simply 'The soup was fine.' — which closed the subject. Emeka acknowledged this dynamic directly: 'Dad always has the final word.' In Session 4, a single line from Chidi ('Emeka. You are coming on Christmas Eve.') ended Emeka's weeks of stalling.

agent_answer: The family chat reveals that **Chidi is the father (Dad) and acts as the authority figure who has the final word in family discussions.** He issues direct instructions to the others — e.g., "Emeka. Confirm your dates" and "Emeka. You are coming on Christmas Eve" — and he decides his own plans: "I will come in March." His son Emeka explicitly acknowledges this role, saying "Dad always has the final word 😊" and repeatedly responds with deferential agreement ("Will do Dad 😊", "Yes Dad 😊 we'll make it work"). Ngozi (the mother) also relays Chidi's wishes to the children ("your father says maybe he will come to London in March"), further confirming that Chidi's announcements set the agenda for the family's plans.
